title: Public Relations
subtitle: Pop Quiz
speaker: Ms Nice
intro: Books away, everyone. Yes, that means you.
Four answers, one clock. Let's see if anybody was listening.

lines: First quiz of the year, so let me walk you through it.
I'll put a question up with four answers underneath it.
Use the arrow keys to move between the four answers.
When you're happy with one, press Z to lock it in.
See that bar? That's your clock.
Answer fast and you'll score more than someone who dithers.
Let it run out and I'll mark it wrong, so guess rather than freeze.
Your running score is up in the corner.
That's the whole game. Off you go.
Pencils down. Let's see the damage.

questions.prompt:
A hero lands a rescue on live television.
What is the FIRST thing they should do?
options: Give a statement to the press
questions.explainRight: Correct. The rescue is the job. The cameras can wait.
questions.explainWrong: The people you just saved come first. Always.

questions.prompt: Public Relations is best described as...
options: Learning to fight in front of a crowd
Managing how the public sees a hero
questions.explainRight: Exactly. Your reputation is a power like any other.
questions.explainWrong: It's about how the public sees you. That's the whole subject.

questions.prompt:
A hero causes property damage stopping a robbery.
What is the right move?
options: Say nothing and hope it blows over
Blame the villain for all of it
Report the damage and help make it right
questions.explainRight: Right. Owning it costs less than being caught hiding it.
questions.explainWrong: Own the damage. A cover-up always costs more than the repair.

questions.prompt: Why does Tungsten High teach PR at all?
options: Heroism is a public, watched profession
questions.explainRight: Yes. Everything you do out there is watched by somebody.
questions.explainWrong: Because the work is public. Someone is always watching.

questions.prompt:
Your friend's power fails badly in front of a crowd.
What do you do?
options: Stand with them and move the crowd on
questions.explainRight: Good. You'll want the same from them one day.
questions.explainWrong: You stand with them. That's the answer I was looking for.

outro: There. That wasn't so bad, was it?
